title: Root-code floors T·r_min for exact root-unit decoders with the dense pairing (sharp on E8, P112, P104, E7, D4, D6), a dense polar law and a place bound (no κ claim)
body:
## Root-code floors T·r_min for exact root-unit decoders with the dense pairing (sharp on E8, P112, P104, E7, D4, D6), a dense polar law and a place bound (no κ claim)

Package `research/ideal-decoder-floors`. Model, cost formula and exact decoders are those of the closed #446 and the merged #595/#1590 and of #2111/#2125; the E8, P112 and P104 floors are those of #620, #717 (D1), #1212, #968, #1077, #1180, #1236, #1744, #1714, re-derived here by one argument. This PR adds the lower-bound side for other units and a derivation of why the block rank is k + 1.

**Place bound (PROVEN, every T).** For every number field, prime 𝔭 | 2 and shift a: cost(B) ≥ |S_a|, the number of lines whose leading 2-adic terms do not cancel (Theorem 1). A tropical argument caps |S_a| by the largest pairwise orthogonal set, ≤ T for Gram decoders M = D₁GD₂ on every even root unit (Proposition 2). The 2-adic/tropical corollary and Lemma VCR2 of #2162 already contain Theorem 1's mechanism (all lines surviving, T = 3) and Proposition 2's cycle condition; no novelty is claimed for that part. **CHECKED:** frame bases attain it (8, 7, 4, 6 on E8, E7, D4, D6), so the ceiling is attained there and far below the optima (8 against 72 on E8, 7 against 49 on E7); a rank-of-sum witness of rank 44 shows that no certificate of the form rank_Q(G∘C) over admissible coverage C (bit model) proves more than 44 for the E8 value 72.

**Dense polar law (PROVEN).** For an odd-or-zero unit the dense pairing is B_ts = Ω(u_t, u_s) with u_t = (1, ℓ_t) and Ω = 1 ⊕ b on F2 ⊕ F2^k, so every term costs at most k + 1, and the rank of a block is an Ω-pairing rank (Theorem 3). This proves the upper bounds behind #968's rule "7 iff both normals are punctured and α·β is odd, else 8" (equalities **CHECKED**: E8, all 14,400 normal pairs: 9 / 8 / 8 / 7), and the rebuilt P104 frame-pair decoder costs 56 = 8 × 7 on 104 live lines (**CHECKED**).

**Root-code floor (PROVEN + CHECKED).** For exact decoders whose two factors lie in the live root code, for the **dense** pairing, over a field of characteristic 0 and **with any number of terms**: cost ≥ T·r_min (Theorem 4; r_min is a minimum over finitely many deficiency types). Sharp, with explicit exact decoders attaining it: **E8 72, P112 64, P104 56, E7 49, E7 minus a 7-frame 42, D4 12, D6 30.** For E7, #2125 found 49 as the first gain (an upper bound); here 49 is a lower bound in this class. For D5 and E6 the pairwise floors are 15 and 30; the forced form N ∝ Gram (CHECKED, N-space of dimension 1; for E6 this is #2137's kernel QG, which has priority) and a coupling lemma give **square decoders ≥ 20 (D5) and ≥ 36 = v (E6)**, from CHECKED incidences (all 27 × 27 deficient E6 pairs are non-orthogonal).

**Scope and caveats.** The floor is for the dense pairing and for root-code factors only; it is **not** a bound over sparser admissible pairings, over factors outside the root code (cf. the 9-term decoder of #1180), over non-Gram geometries, or over overcomplete E6 (m = 7: 35 < 36 not excluded) and D5. Conjecture ID (cost* = min(v, T(k+1) − usable deficiencies)) is a conjecture; it matches the ten values on record (each in its stated scope). Forced triangular minors (#2176's tool) give only 7 per co-flat E8 term. Where the place bound is stated for every T it extends #2162's 2-adic/tropical corollary and the reduction-mod-2 idea of #1590/#2017; the new content is the count |S_a|, the ceiling and the root-code results. Open next questions (non-dense B, factors outside the root code, overcomplete E6 m = 7 / D5 m = 6, T = 3) are listed in README §6. No κ claim, no window closed, no supplier changed.

**Verify.** `bash research/ideal-decoder-floors/verify.sh /fresh/dir` (Python standard library only, single process, no SAT; step 0 checks `MANIFEST.sha256` and `SOURCES.json` and stops hard on mismatch; 66 PASS lines including step 0).
